analysis.title: The Reflexive Warsh Put: Goldman Says A Stock Slide Is The Only Thing That Stops The Hikes
key_insights: Goldman's Privorotsky says equities are pricing a growth scare that bonds have not acknowledged. Utilities (XLU) outperformed long Treasuries (TLT) by roughly 5 percentage points over 20 sessions, a 3 standard deviation gap.
Privorotsky's Fed read: if equities keep falling, the distribution of rate outcomes should shift quickly away from hikes. The article concludes the bond rally comes only after stocks break.

The article says Fed Chair Warsh has a history of focusing on financial conditions (FCI). It cites his Monday remarks describing an AI disappointment scenario in which equity valuations fall and unemployment rises.

The article says Warsh hiked in a way consistent with Goldman's September call that he would not want to disappoint the market. It infers he would not sit still if the market fell sharply. The strike of the put is described as lower than today's level, with no Fed official saying how much lower.
Hawkish Fed voices persist. Cleveland's Hammack still prefers steady and slow rate hikes, and Williams stressed policy must stay sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2%.

US export-control tightening hit Asia's AI supply chain. A Commerce interim rule now requires a US license to export advanced AI chips to data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. The Kospi broke below 5,000 and the Taiex closed down 2.3%.

The MATCH Act would give allies such as the Netherlands and Japan 150 days to match US chipmaking equipment controls. The RASA bill, passed by the House in January, would let Commerce stop Chinese firms renting overseas data centers to reach Nvidia hardware. Lawmakers aim to attach the four-bill package to the NDAA.
Jensen Huang's departure removes the industry's most effective lobbyist against tighter chip rules. House Speaker Johnson cited a growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China.

Asian cross-currents on the export news: China's domestic AI basket rose 1.69% on the bet that curbs speed up domestic chips, Alibaba fell nearly 5%, Korea saw $1 billion of foreign selling ($806 million in tech), and India rallied a fifth straight session on record foreign inflows.

Monday's US tape was defensive. The S&P fell 1.9% to 7,420, the Nasdaq 100 lost 2.5%, and every sector except consumer staples fell. Oil fell about 4% while the long end of the bond market barely moved.

Nvidia reports after the close Tuesday, its first print under interim CEO Colette Kress, with the stock down about 30% over six straight weeks. Privorotsky suspects near-term numbers could be robust but says the market has no idea what multiple to put on 2028 to 2030 earnings.
Technical level: the recent Nasdaq 100 lows are the line in the sand. Holding allows a base to form. A break risks another mechanical leg lower as CTAs sell, volatility rises and risk is reduced.

Privorotsky expects cyber budgets to behave like non-discretionary capex after Monday's banking-app IT outages and Friday's United Airlines ground stop, none confirmed as cyberattacks. He says more spending feels baked for 2027-30. He also flags robotics as an under-discussed AI theme.

The article's own view is that equities are right and bonds are late. It notes US and European 10-year yields were down three to four basis points at press time, which Bloomberg called a rotation into bonds.

geopolitical: US Commerce Department interim rule requires a license to export advanced AI chips to data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent overseas compute.
The MATCH Act would give allies such as the Netherlands and Japan 150 days to match US controls on chipmaking equipment or face the same restrictions.
The Remote Access Security Act (RASA), passed by the House in January, would give Commerce statutory power to stop Chinese firms renting overseas data centers to reach Nvidia hardware.
Lawmakers aim to attach the four-bill chip export package to the NDAA, with Speaker Johnson citing a growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China.
The article reads the curbs as boosting Beijing's chip self-sufficiency drive, with the costs falling on Taiwan, South Korea and Thailand.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities are right: the article argues the slowdown is real and bonds are simply late, with 10-year yields starting to fall at press time.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates and FX are not confirming. Long bonds barely rallied on oil down, stocks down and growth down, so either equities are overreacting or rates and FX are underreacting.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the recent Nasdaq 100 lows without a bond rally would show the pessimistic equity read is not confirmed by rates.

tension_points.bull_case: If the recent NDX lows hold, a base can form.
tension_points.bear_case: A break risks another mechanical leg lower as CTAs sell, volatility rises and risk is reduced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the recent Nasdaq 100 lows invalidates the base-forming case.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh focuses on financial conditions and described an AI bust scenario, so a falling equity market should pull rate outcomes away from hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Williams and Hammack remain hawkish, and Warsh said productivity has not yet broken out structurally to the upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued hawkish Fed speak despite a clear break in equities would undercut the put.
